name: Input Injection
description:
A malicious application can inject input to the user interface to mimic user interaction through the abuse of Android's accessibility APIs.

[Input Injection](https://attack.mitre.org/techniques/T1516) can be achieved using any of the following methods:

* Mimicking user clicks on the screen, for example to steal money from a user's PayPal account.(Citation: android-trojan-steals-paypal-2fa)
* Injecting global actions, such as `GLOBAL_ACTION_BACK` (programatically mimicking a physical back button press), to trigger actions on behalf of the user.(Citation: Talos Gustuff Apr 2019)
* Inserting input into text fields on behalf of the user. This method is used legitimately to auto-fill text fields by applications such as password managers.(Citation: bitwarden autofill logins)

references.description: Bitwarden. (n.d.).  Auto-fill logins on Android . Retrieved September 15, 2019.
Lukáš Štefanko. (2018, December 11). Android Trojan steals money from PayPal accounts even with 2FA on. Retrieved July 11, 2019.
Vitor Ventura. (2019, April 9).  Gustuff banking botnet targets Australia . Retrieved September 3, 2019.

telemetry.name: Application State
telemetry.description: Application state and lifecycle observations such as foreground/background transitions.
telemetry.collection_focus: Instrument the owned app lifecycle and corroborate permitted service snapshots; distinguish app events from inferred gateway activity.

providers.name: Android logcat
providers.scope: Permitted logs from a consented test device/emulator; output depends on build, permissions and instrumentation.

providers.name: Android dumpsys
providers.scope: Point-in-time service/package state on an authorized development device.

providers.name: Instrumented test application
providers.scope: Own-app permission, API and state callbacks; not universal visibility into other apps.

configuration: Use a disposable emulator or owned development device with approved debugging. Record OS/API level, app version and instrumentation privileges.
Collect only relevant logcat buffers/tags and service snapshots; add explicit own-app instrumentation for events absent from OS logs.
Forward sanitized logs and compare before/after state. Remove test data and revoke debugging access after the lab session.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Android tooling does not imply iOS coverage. Standard mobile apps cannot observe all other apps or protected OS internals; MDM status is not full API, filesystem or content telemetry.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Per owned device, app version and permission state: unexpected API/permission changes, background activity and network destinations. OS privacy restrictions and emulator differences limit observability.

telemetry.name: OS API Execution
telemetry.description: Instrumented operating-system API calls and their return values.
telemetry.collection_focus: Use an approved EDR trace or instrument the owned lab process at selected APIs. Define API name, caller, sanitized arguments and return status.

providers.name: Application audit logs
providers.scope: First-party service events and request/result fields; schema is application-specific.

providers.name: OpenTelemetry-compatible log pipelines
providers.scope: Transport and normalization of emitted records; do not create missing audit instrumentation.

configuration: Enable the application audit category or instrument the owned lab application at the authorization/action boundary.
Define a schema with timestamp, service, actor, object, action, result and correlation ID. Export structured records through an authenticated collector.
Redact secrets and personal content, separate audit from debug logs, set retention and verify delivery during rotation/restart.
telemetry.example_note: Project-normalized synthetic JSON, not a native provider log, captured event, attack verdict or validated detection. A parser/adapter is required for a real SIEM. Example names, IPs and values are fictional.
telemetry.limitations: Debug output is not necessarily a durable audit trail. Application developers must emit the relevant event; installing a log pipeline does not make an absent event exist.
telemetry.anomaly_design: Per application, client and route: request rate, rare actions, failure ratios and unusual state transitions. Version changes, retries, health probes and seasonal load need separate baselines.

analytics.name: Analytic 1666
analytics.guidance: The defender correlates Android accessibility or UI-automation-capable behavior from an app identity with injected user-interface actions occurring on behalf of the user in another foreground application. The strongest Android evidence is accessibility-enabled or similarly privileged app behavior that triggers programmatic clicks, global actions, or text insertion into another app's active UI, especially when those actions occur without matching user touch interaction, while the injecting app is backgrounded or foreground-service-only, or when the target foreground app belongs to a sensitive category such as banking, payments, identity, communications, or enterprise access. The detection is strengthened when the injected input sequence is followed by target-app navigation, form submission, transaction progression, or network activity from the target context.

tuning.description: Correlation window linking injected actions to target-app navigation, submission, or downstream network effects.
Approved accessibility, autofill, remote-assist, or QA/testing apps vary by organization and device group.
Approved accessibility-enabled apps vary by assistive and enterprise workflow.
Approved password managers or autofill-capable apps may legitimately inject text into fields.
Defines how close an injected action must be to user interaction to be considered expected.
Categories such as banking, payments, identity, communications, and enterprise access may warrant higher sensitivity.
Threshold for repeated programmatic global actions within a short window.
Minimum inserted text length or field-population pattern considered suspicious outside approved autofill workflows.
Grace period allowed after explicit user enablement of approved accessibility or autofill workflows before injection is treated as suspicious.

log_sources.name: MobileEDR:telemetry
log_sources.channel: Accessibility-enabled app invoked programmatic click or action on behalf of user while a different app was foregrounded and injected action was not mapped to approved accessibility or autofill workflow

log_sources.name: MobileEDR:telemetry
log_sources.channel: Accessibility-enabled app invoked global action such as back, home, recents, or navigation control while target foreground app context changed within TimeWindow

log_sources.name: MobileEDR:telemetry
log_sources.channel: Accessibility-enabled app inserted text into active field of different foreground app without user keyboard activity or approved autofill relationship

log_sources.name: MobileEDR:telemetry
log_sources.channel: Injecting app remained backgrounded or foreground-service-only while injected click, global action, or text insertion occurred in a different foreground app

log_sources.name: MobileEDR:telemetry
log_sources.channel: LastUserInteractionDelta exceeded threshold before injected UI action and no matching touch interaction was observed for the target foreground app during injection sequence

log_sources.name: MobileEDR:telemetry
log_sources.channel: Sensitive app category remained foregrounded during injected UI sequence from different app identity

software.name: Riltok
software.description: [Riltok](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0403) injects input to set itself as the default SMS handler by clicking the appropriate places on the screen. It can also close or minimize targeted antivirus applications and the device security settings screen.(Citation: Kaspersky Riltok June 2019)

references.description: Tatyana Shishkova. (2019, June 25). Riltok mobile Trojan: A banker with global reach. Retrieved August 7, 2019.

software.name: Gustuff
software.description: [Gustuff](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0406) injects the global action `GLOBAL_ACTION_BACK` to mimic pressing the back button to close the application if a call to an open antivirus application is detected.(Citation: Talos Gustuff Apr 2019)

references.description: Vitor Ventura. (2019, April 9).  Gustuff banking botnet targets Australia . Retrieved September 3, 2019.

software.name: Ginp
software.description: [Ginp](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0423) can inject input to make itself the default SMS handler.(Citation: ThreatFabric Ginp)

references.description: ThreatFabric. (2019, November). Ginp - A malware patchwork borrowing from Anubis. Retrieved April 8, 2020.

software.name: TrickMo
software.description: [TrickMo](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0427) can inject input to set itself as the default SMS handler, and to automatically click through pop-ups without giving the user any time to react.(Citation: SecurityIntelligence TrickMo)

references.description: P. Asinovsky. (2020, March 24). TrickBot Pushing a 2FA Bypass App to Bank Customers in Germany. Retrieved April 24, 2020.

software.name: DEFENSOR ID
software.description: [DEFENSOR ID](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0479) can abuse the accessibility service to perform actions on behalf of the user, including launching attacker-specified applications to steal data.(Citation: ESET DEFENSOR ID)

references.description: L. Stefanko. (2020, May 22). Insidious Android malware gives up all malicious features but one to gain stealth. Retrieved June 26, 2020.

software.name: Cerberus
software.description: [Cerberus](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0480) can inject input to grant itself additional permissions without user interaction and to prevent application removal.(Citation: Threat Fabric Cerberus)(Citation: CheckPoint Cerberus)

software.name: Mandrake
software.description: [Mandrake](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0485) abuses the accessibility service to prevent removing administrator permissions, accessibility permissions, and to set itself as the default SMS handler.(Citation: Bitdefender Mandrake)

references.description: R. Gevers, M. Tivadar, R. Bleotu, A. M. Barbatei, et al.. (2020, May 14). Uprooting Mandrake: The Story of an Advanced Android Spyware Framework That Went Undetected for 4 Years. Retrieved July 15, 2020.

software.name: Zen
software.description: [Zen](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0494) can simulate user clicks on ads and system prompts to create new Google accounts.(Citation: Google Security Zen)

references.description: Siewierski, L. (2019, January 11). PHA Family Highlights: Zen and its cousins . Retrieved July 27, 2020.

software.name: TERRACOTTA
software.description: [TERRACOTTA](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S0545) can inject clicks to launch applications, share posts on social media, and interact with WebViews to perform fraudulent actions.(Citation: WhiteOps TERRACOTTA)

software.name: SharkBot
software.description: [SharkBot](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S1055) can use input injection via Accessibility Services to simulate user touch inputs, prevent applications from opening, change device settings, and bypass MFA protections.(Citation: nccgroup_sharkbot_0322)

software.name: Crocodilus
software.description: [Crocodilus](https://attack.mitre.org/software/S9004) has the ability to perform clicks, swipes (left, right, up and down) on the screen and actions such as “Back,” “Home,” and “Menu.”(Citation: ThreatFabric_Crocodilus_March2025)

mitigations.name: User Guidance
mitigations.description: Users should be warned against granting access to accessibility features, and to carefully scrutinize applications that request this dangerous permission.

mitigations.name: Enterprise Policy
mitigations.description: An EMM/MDM can use the Android `DevicePolicyManager.setPermittedAccessibilityServices` method to set an explicit list of applications that are allowed to use Android's accessibility features.

simulation.prerequisites: Use owned test devices or emulators, disposable app accounts and test data. Verify platform/version instrumentation; desktop test procedures do not establish mobile coverage.

synthetic.purpose: Collection/parser contract exercise, NOT a positive example or detection of this TTP.
